query: What signals suggest a travel expense will be declined?

per_column.name: has_processed_date
per_column.rationale: Whether a processed_date exists is a post-outcome artifact of the expense being processed/adjudicated. A declined expense's processing status is tied to reaching a terminal state, so this indicator is knowable only after (or as part of) the outcome and leaks the resolution rather than predicting it ex ante.

per_column.name: is_customer_support_travel
per_column.rationale: Derived from department/context, this flags a specific requesting group. Department is a legitimate ex-ante attribute known at submission and can plausibly carry signal about approval/decline rates, lying outside the focus variable.

per_column.name: is_sales_travel
per_column.rationale: Same as above: a pre-outcome categorical indicator of the submitting group/travel type. Known before adjudication and plausibly correlated with decline likelihood without restating or leaking the outcome.

judge.rationale: Two of the three columns (department/travel-type indicators) are legitimate ex-ante predictors, though they are one-hot restatements of the already-present 'department'/'category' fields and thus add limited leverage beyond the original table. The has_processed_date flag leaks the outcome since processing status is a post-adjudication artifact. As a set, modest genuine predictive signal, discounted for redundancy with existing columns and one leaking feature.
